ic_name: LIN bus 2.2A (Local Interconnect Network, LIN Consortium)
base_address: Defined at SoC level; offsets given relative to module base.
notes: Where this Phase-1 LRM expects 'registers', the LIN protocol provides 'fields and tables'. The register-level mapping is left to the implementer.
rationale: LIN is a wire-level protocol specification, not a chip. The spec does not define a host-CPU register map. Implementations build on top of an existing UART/SCI peripheral (or a pure state machine) on a microcontroller; the register map at that level is vendor-specific (e.g. NXP / Renesas / Microchip / TI LIN-capable UARTs).
implementation_register_groups_required_: UART/SCI: baud-rate divisor, parity = none, data bits = 8, stop bits = 1, LSB-first.
Break generator / detector: ≥13 bit-time dominant TX break; ≥11 bit-time dominant RX detect threshold.
Schedule table memory (master only): a list of (slot_index, frame_id, slot_duration, type) entries.
Frame table (master + slave): per-frame entry { ID, direction (publish/subscribe), length, checksum model, callback }.
NAD register (slave only): initial NAD (from LDF) + current NAD assignable via Assign NAD service.
Supplier ID, Function ID, Variant (slave only): published in Read by Identifier service.
Status / response_error register (slave): 1-bit signal published in one of the slave's unconditional frames; set on any non-event-triggered frame response error.

diagnostic_pdu_layout.byte1: PCI (Protocol Control Information): bits 7:4 = PDU type code (SF=0x0, FF=0x1, CF=0x2), bits 3:0 = length (SF) or sequence number (CF) or upper nibble of length (FF).
diagnostic_pdu_layout.byte2_if_SF_or_FF: SF: LEN (1..6); FF: lower 8 bits of total LEN (LEN 7..4095).
diagnostic_pdu_layout.byte4_to_byte7_if_SF: D1..D5 service data (last bytes padded 0xFF if unused)
